get.description: Retrieves the list of all Outbound Email DLP rules. You can filter the results based on rule attributes.

parameters.name: orgId
parameters.description: The unique identifier for the organization.

post.description: Creates a new Outbound Email DLP rule. To learn more, see Configuring Outbound Email DLP Policy Rules.

get.description: Gets the list of all Outbound Email DLP rules with limited information about each rule. To get complete rule details, use the GET /emailDlpRules request.

put.description: Updates information for an existing Outbound Email DLP rule. To learn more, see Configuring Outbound Email DLP Policy Rules

parameters.description: The unique identifier for the rule

delete.description: Deletes an Outbound Email DLP rule based on the specified rule ID

parameters.name: ruleId
parameters.description: The unique identifier for the rule

EmailDlpRule.description: Outbound Email DLP policy rule configuration details. To learn more, see Configuring Outbound Email DLP Policy Rules.

id.description: A unique, system-generated identifier for the rule

order.description: The order of execution of the rule with respect to other rules

action.description: Action to be applied when traffic matches the rule conditions

groups.description: Name-ID pairs of user groups to which the rule applies. If no value is set, this criterion is not considered for rule match.

departments.description: Name-ID pairs of departments to which the rule applies. If no value is set, this criterion is not considered for rule match.

users.description: Name-ID pairs of users to which the rule applies. If no value is set, this criterion is not considered for rule match.

excludedGroups.description: Name-ID pairs of user groups that are excluded from your Outbound Email DLP policy. This field is used in configuring exception rules, which are child rules that allow excluding specific users or groups in your organization that must perform tasks as part of a necessary workflow that might otherwise violate outbound email policy.

excludedDepartments.description: Name-ID pairs of departments that are excluded from your Outbound Email DLP policy. This field is used in configuring exception rules, which are child rules that allow excluding specific users or groups in your organization that must perform tasks as part of a necessary workflow that might otherwise violate outbound email policy.

excludedUsers.description: Name-ID pairs of users that are excluded from your Outbound Email DLP policy. This field is used in configuring exception rules, which are child rules that allow excluding specific users or groups in your organization that must perform tasks as part of a necessary workflow that might otherwise violate outbound email policy.

timeWindows.description: List of time intervals during which the rule is enforced

dlpEngines.description: DLP engines that scan the content. If no value is set, all DLP engines are selected implicitly.

fileTypes.description: File type categories to which the rule applies. If no value is set, this criterion is not considered for rule match.

minSize.description: Minimum size requirement (in KB) that data must meet before the rule applies. The default minimum data size is O KB (i.e., there is no minimum data size requirement).

withoutContentInspection.description: A Boolean value when set to true indicates that external DLP engine is used. The Zscaler service doesn't use DLP engines to scan the content; instead, the service functions as a filter, only flagging content based on the specified criteria.

auditor.description: Specifies auditor information if an email notification must be configured for the rule. Use this field if the auditor is from a hosted database. If you do not specify the auditor and select a notification template, a notification is not sent for this rule.

externalAuditorEmail.description: Specifies auditor information if an email notification must be configured for the rule. Use this field if the auditor is external and specify the auditor's email address. If you do not specify the auditor and select a notification template, a notification is not sent for this rule.

notificationTemplate.description: Specifies the notification template to use for the rule

lastModifiedTime.description: Timestamp when the rule was last modified

lastModifiedBy.description: Admin user that last modified the rule

receiver.description: Details of the Zscaler Incident Receiver that is applicable

labels.description: Name-ID pairs of the labels associated with the rule

includedDomainProfiles.description: List of domain profiles that are included in the rule criteria

severity.description: Severity level of the policy rule violation

userRiskScoreLevels.description: User risk score levels to which the policy rule applies

emailTenants.description: Email tenants to which the rule applies

contentLocations.description: Specifies where the Zscaler service should look for sensitive data (e.g., email attachments, email body, or email subject)

parentRule.description: Parent rule ID applicable when configuring exception rules

customHeader.description: Policy action to include a custom header on emails that trigger this rule. Custom headers are designed to take an action that is mapped to the header on the email server. Custom Header format: X-name:value, where 0=Allow and 1=Block (e.g., X-Zscaler-Encrypt:1).

emailRecipientProfiles.description: Recipient profiles to which the rule applies

id.description: A unique identifier for an entity

name.description: The configured name of the entity

externalId.description: An external identifier used for an entity that is managed outside of ZIA. Examples include zpaServerGroup and zpaAppSegments. This field is not applicable to ZIA-managed entities.

EntityReference.description: This is an immutable reference to an entity that mainly consists of id and name

IncidentReceiverReference.description: Information about a About Zscaler Incident Receiver

EmailDlpSubRule.description: Outbound Email DLP policy exception rule configuration details. Exception rules allow you to exclude specific users or groups in your organization that need to perform tasks as part of a necessary workflow that might otherwise violate outbound email policy rules. The exception rules automatically inherit the rule name from the parent rule, but you can customize other exception rule settings. To learn more, see Configuring Outbound Email DLP Policy Rules.

id.description: A unique, system-generated identifier for the exeception rule

order.description: All parent rules are evaluated. If multiple rules match, the rule with the most restrictive action and highest rule order is applied. Exception rule evaluation stops at the first match, and an exception replaces a parent rule upon match.

name.description: The rule name is inherited from the parent rule and cannot be modified

description.description: Additional information about the exception rule

state.description: Rule enablement status. An enabled exception rule is actively enforced. A disabled exception rule is not actively enforced but does not lose its place in the rule order; the service skips it and moves to the next exception rule.

action.description: Action to be applied when traffic matches the exception rule conditions

groups.description: Name-ID pairs of user groups to which the exception rule applies. If no value is set, this criterion is not considered for rule match.

departments.description: Name-ID pairs of departments to which the exception rule applies. If no value is set, this criterion is not considered for rule match.

users.description: Name-ID pairs of users to which the exception rule applies. If no value is set, this criterion is not considered for rule match.

excludedGroups.description: Name-ID pairs of user groups that are excluded from your Outbound Email DLP policy. This field is used in configuring exception rules, which are child rules that allow excluding specific users or groups in your organization that must perform tasks as part of a necessary workflow that might otherwise violate outbound email policy.

excludedDepartments.description: Name-ID pairs of departments that are excluded from your Outbound Email DLP policy. This field is used in configuring exception rules, which are child rules that allow excluding specific users or groups in your organization that must perform tasks as part of a necessary workflow that might otherwise violate outbound email policy.

excludedUsers.description: Name-ID pairs of users that are excluded from your Outbound Email DLP policy. This field is used in configuring exception rules, which are child rules that allow excluding specific users or groups in your organization that must perform tasks as part of a necessary workflow that might otherwise violate outbound email policy.

timeWindows.description: List of time intervals during which the exception rule is enforced

dlpEngines.description: DLP engines that must be used for content inspection. A maximum of 4 DLP engines can be specified explicitly. If no value is set, all DLP engines are selected implicitly. Content Matching must be enabled for the rule to select DLP engines.

fileTypes.description: File type categories to which the exception rule applies. If no value is set, this criterion is not considered for rule match.

minSize.description: Minimum size requirement (in KB) that data must meet before the rule applies. The default minimum data size is O KB (i.e., there is no minimum data size requirement).

withoutContentInspection.description: A Boolean value when set to true indicates that external DLP engine is used. The Zscaler service doesn't use DLP engines to scan the content; instead, the service functions as a filter, only flagging content based on the specified criteria.

auditor.description: Specifies auditor information if an email notification must be configured for the rule. Use this field if the auditor is from a hosted database. You can retrieve auditor information using the GET /users/auditors request. If you do not specify the auditor and select a notification template, a notification is not sent for this rule.

externalAuditorEmail.description: Specifies auditor information if an email notification must be configured for the rule. Use this field if the auditor is external and specify the auditor's email address. If you do not specify the auditor and select a notification template, a notification is not sent for this rule.

notificationTemplate.description: Specifies the notification template to use for the exception rule

lastModifiedTime.description: Timestamp when the exception rule was last modified

lastModifiedBy.description: Admin user that last modified the exception rule

receiver.description: Details of the Zscaler Incident Receiver that is applicable

labels.description: Name-ID pairs of the labels associated with the exception rule

includedDomainProfiles.description: List of domain profiles that are included in the rule criteria

severity.description: Severity level of the exception rule violation

userRiskScoreLevels.description: User risk score levels to which the exception rule applies

emailTenants.description: Email tenants to which the exception rule applies

contentLocations.description: Specifies where the Zscaler service should look for sensitive data (e.g., email attachments, email body, or email subject)

parentRule.description: Parent rule ID for the exception rule. This field is required when configuring an exception rule.

customHeader.description: Policy action to include a custom header on emails that trigger this rule. Custom headers are designed to take an action that is mapped to the header on the email server. Custom Header format: X-name:value, where 0=Allow and 1=Block (e.g., X-Zscaler-Encrypt:1).

emailRecipientProfiles.description: Recipient profiles to which the rule applies
